interpretation: The observed regression is retained: the same 240-interval pump workload takes longer and the same 153-action UI burst has larger queue/presentation tails. No performance equivalence to the superseded baseline is claimed.

Headless pump profiles do not instantiate the repaired owner scene. They retain identical script/runtime interface inputs, canonical publications, accounting, cadence target and workload counts; native execution, snapshot and value-accounting medians rose in the new actual run.

All 6,075,904 actual DLL bytes compared. Only a temporary export-filename suffix and CodeView build identity differ; no executable instruction or numerical constant delta was observed. Fresh exact-source compilation and custody are independently established.

Same pinned engine and selected Rapier, same reported software renderer, but resource sampling is unavailable in both Windows trials. There is no retained CPU utilization, host scheduling or hardware evidence that proves a cause.

Inference only: broad measured per-stage cost increases and extra callback cycles are compatible with execution-cost/scheduling differences; these trials do not establish runner variance or causation by the navigation changes.

Unchanged registered Lab limits still pass. These do not constrain the new burst input latency. The observed 1.9-second tail remains a practical limitation for owner evaluation; no 60 FPS or universally responsive editing claim is supported.

No additional campaign was commissioned: existing evidence identifies the actual stage/cadence difference and the limits of attribution without weakening budgets or treating a repeated trial as a replacement.
status: investigated; negative timing drift retained; causal attribution unresolved
